$comment: Lighthouse CI budget gate for apps/site. Runnable locally: `pnpm -F site
build` then `pnpm -F site lighthouse` (it starts its own production server).
Wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml as steps on the existing `ci` job,
path-gated on apps/site/**.
WINDOWS: `lhci autorun` exits 1 on Windows inside chrome-launcher's temp-dir
cleanup (EPERM removing %TEMP%\lighthouse.*). That happens AFTER the report
is written, so the reports are valid — it is an upstream chrome-launcher bug,
not a gate failure. CI is ubuntu-latest and unaffected. To measure on Windows,
run the lighthouse CLI yourself into .lighthouseci/lhr-<digits>.json (ignoring
its exit code) and then `npx lhci assert`.
Design notes, because the failure mode to avoid here is a flaky check people
learn to click past:
- Runs against a LOCAL production build (next start), never the deployed
site. CI must not depend on Railway being up, and must grade the PR's
code rather than whatever happens to be live.
- numberOfRuns 3 + aggregationMethod median. Lighthouse scores are noisy;
the median of three is what gets asserted. LHCI's DEFAULT is
`optimistic` — the BEST run — which would hide real regressions.
- Category floors are set below what the code currently measures, not at
the aspirational targets, so the gate is green on the commit that adds it
and only fires on an actual slide. Measured on this branch (median of 3,
desktop preset, localhost): performance 98, accessibility 89, seo 100,
best-practices 100.
- ACCESSIBILITY IS NOT AT ITS TARGET. Issue #255 wants 94; the code scores
89.4 and four weighted audits are still failing on `/`:
aria-progressbar-name (w7 — that is issue #255's OTHER item, a
packages/core Progress fix), color-contrast (w7), target-size (w7),
heading-order (w3). Applicable weight is 226, of which 202 passes. Fixing
any one of the w7 audits moves the category to ~92.5; all four reach 100.
The floor here is deliberately 0.88 so the gate is honest and blocking
today — RAISE IT as those audits get fixed.
- The specific audits from #255 are asserted individually. They are binary
pass/fail, not scored heuristics, so they do not drift and there is no
noise argument for softening them.
- non-composited-animations is asserted with maxLength (item count), NOT
minScore. In Lighthouse 12 that audit reports scoreDisplayMode
'informative' with score hard-set to 1 even when it lists offenders, so a
minScore assertion passes while the page is full of them. maxLength reads
details.items.length, which is the real signal. Verified: it was 29
before the hero-stroke rewrite and is 0 after.
- total-byte-weight is the guard for the <audio preload> class of
regression. Measured 1.45MB; budget 2.5MB. Re-adding a ~4.7MB hot-linked
media fetch blows straight through it. (uses-rel-preconnect was NOT used:
it audits preconnect hints to critical origins, which has nothing to do
with over-fetching bytes.)
- Only `/` is measured. That is where all four #255 regressions live, and
each extra URL costs 3 more Lighthouse runs. Add URLs to collect.url when
a specific page earns the runtime.
